Constantine wins one of them, becomes emperor, and moves the capital from Rome all the way to Constantinople, establishing a new culture called the Byzantine Empire.

The Byzantines call themselves Romans but are more like Greeks. Another major difference is that Rome is in Western Europe, while Constantinople is off in Eastern Europe. Now, Rome can defend its wealthy provinces of Anatolia and Egypt much more effectively because Constantinople is by the sea and has high walls making it almost impossible to invade.

The Hag Sophia, the official church of this new religion, is called Eastern Orthodox today but was then just part of the Catholic Church. At its peak, Constantinople is very wealthy, surrounded by seawalls that make it nearly impregnable, standing for about a thousand years. The Council of Nicaea makes the Holy Trinity the official doctrine of the Catholic Church, and even today Christians still recite it as the Nicene Creed.

The Nicene Creed establishes the idea that Jesus, God, and the Holy Spirit are separate but one and the same, different yet co-equal. If you study this creed closely, you'll find inconsistencies: Jesus is a son of God but also one with God. This doesn't make much sense but is something you must memorize; it's like a math formula.
